newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PEARCE OFFERED CARETAKER ROLE AT FOREST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PEARCE OFFERED CARETAKER ROLE AT FOREST.

text.p: England defender Stuart Pearce has been offered the role of caretaker manager at struggling Nottingham Forest following the resignation of Frank Clark on Thursday.
The English premier league's bottom club have given Pearce, capped 72 times by his country, 24 hours to decide whether to take the job.
"If he doesn't accept we'll think again," said chairman Irving Korn. "But I think that Stuart, being the type of person he is, will accept the challenge."

The 53-year-old Clark, who took over from Brian Clough in May 1993, had grown increasingly frustrated as protracted takeover negotiations prevented the club from signing new players to improve a sequence of poor results.

Forest have not won since the opening day of the season and their 4-2 defeat at Liverpool on Tuesday proved the final straw for Clark, who suspected he would be sacked anyway once the club's takeover is finalised in the New Year.

"I believed I would be out like a shot and I didn't want to be sitting around like a turkey waiting for Christmas," said Clark. "I don't feel I can do anything else for the players to get them out of this mess. Going will do them a favour. They might just get the couple of results they desperately need."

In Clark's first season, Forest won promotion back to the premier league and a year later they qualified for Europe, reaching the quarter-finals of the UEFA Cup last season before going out to Bayern Munich.

As a player, Clark won a UEFA Cup winners medal in 1969 with Newcastle before moving to Forest where he collected a league championship medal in 1978, two League Cups and the European Cup in 1979 at the age of 35. He has already been linked with the managerial vacancy at Manchester City.
